Take care of a class job
Friday 4 December 2026 · one 40-minute lesson · Year A
Term theme: Identity & Belonging
Thread tags: SMSC S/So (M/C: none); British Values IL/MR (D/RL/T: none).
Objective

Source: scheme_references/BUILD_SOW.xlsx; BUILD Weekly - Autumn, C141. Independence / vocational strand; Friday slot confirmed by the owner.
Big question and success checks
How will I know my job is done?
Find out what the job needs. Do the job with care and ask for help. Check the result and report back.
Evidence

VOCATIONAL-BUILD-A2-W05-E1: A dated observation of each learner preparing a work tray, checking it against the job card and reporting ready or a remaining need; actual actions, prompts, adult help and a next step are recorded.
Prepare

Prepare one light work tray per learner, plain sheets, suitable pencils and printed help cards. Keep supplies within easy reach. Set an accessible place for each finished tray and a separate adult model tray. Plan the real follow-on task: each learner uses a prepared tray to draw one simple shape or make a chosen mark; the help card is available to request support. Print the two Evidence Sheet and two Support Cards pages and a Vocabulary Mat.
Calendar and progression
Year A. Autumn 2 Week 5: 30 November–4 December 2026. Friday 4 December 2026, one 40-minute taught lesson. No clock time is specified. Weeks 1–6 are formative; Week 7 is assessing.
Week 5 applies familiar skills to a real class job. Week 6 prepares a seasonal craft item, using a plan, supported making and a check. The community-project strand is not used.

This helps me finish a job, check it and report back.
Teaching sequence
Slide
Min
Teaching action
Read the objective, big question, theme and careers line.
Offer a pause, usual aid and agreed help.
Show the real follow-on task and the three-item kit list.
Read the objective and three success checks.
Use the separate adult tray. Model reading the job, placing three items, checking and reporting.
Use the missing-help-card hinge and the missing-pencil parallel recheck.
Each learner prepares one real work tray, checks it and reports its status. Observe actions and support.
Record the job and check. Use each prepared tray for a brief chosen-mark task; the help card is available.
Give one prompt; record a changed check or report. Return kit after use and store the work.
Ask how the learner knew the job was ready and what they would do if an item was missing.
Keep the word mat visible and explain words in the task.
Hidden staff brief: clear finish point, safe materials and individual evidence.
Hinge response and reteach

The adult tray has a sheet and a pencil but no help card. Ask: “Is the job ready, or is something missing?” Expected: notice the help card; add it if available or tell the adult it is needed. If unsure, point to the job list, ask a short question, rephrase, offer a choice and model only the first needed action. Parallel recheck: a tray has a sheet and help card but no pencil.
Routes

Supported: Read one part of the job card at a time. Offer the required items within reach, a point or aid, and an adapted way to place them. Record prompts and adult actions; keep the learner’s own contribution clear.
Independent: Use the full job card to collect the three items, check the tray and report ready or a need. Use the usual adult safety supervision and record any help requested.

Aspire: Complete the same job, explain how the check helped and spot a missing item in the separate adult tray. Suggest a way to make the next set-up clearer without taking over another learner’s work.
Safe teaching and evidence
Boundaries and practical support

Agree a small, safe class job with a clear finish point. Use light trays and ordinary checked stationery in an accessible work area. Adults manage any heavy item, high storage, spill or unsafe equipment. Do not use personal records or real names. A request for help is a responsible action, not failure. Respect a pause or adapted role; record what the learner did and what an adult completed. A group result does not prove that each learner completed the job.

Give each learner one tray and a clear reachable supply area. Observe collecting, placing, checking and reporting individually. Offer the prompt ladder and usual aid. Record the learner’s actions separately from adult completion. Allow a responsible report of an unfinished need; do not treat a polished tray as the only evidence.
Keep unobserved actions or unpresented cards as gaps. Record reading, reduced choices, prompts, models and adult actions. A group answer is not individual evidence.
Evidence and feedback
A dated observation of each learner preparing a work tray, checking it against the job card and reporting ready or a remaining need; actual actions, prompts, adult help and a next step are recorded.

Staff answers and observation
Take care of a class job
These are teaching guides, not prefilled learner evidence. Use a separate adult model. Record actual responses, actions and support.
Model and task key

My job is to set up one work tray. I read the list: one sheet, pencil and help card. I put the three items on the tray. I check each item against the list. I put the tray in the agreed place. I tell the adult it is ready, or say what I need.
Part
Teaching guide
Job brief
One work tray needs one plain sheet, one suitable pencil and one help card. Agree the destination and accessible method of placing the tray before starting.
Check
Compare the actual tray with all three listed items. A missing item is reported or added safely. Checking is observed, not inferred from a finished tray.
Report
Accept ready, a point to the checked list, an aid response or a clear request for the missing item. Record actual communication.
Real purpose
Use the trays during the evidence stage for a brief mark-making task. This makes resource preparation a real class job. Drawing quality and speed are not assessed.
Responsibility
Starting, caring for kit, checking and reporting a need can all show responsibility. Asking for help is appropriate; it does not cancel the learner’s contribution.
Hinge and reteach

The adult tray has a sheet and a pencil but no help card. Ask: “Is the job ready, or is something missing?” Expected: notice the help card; add it if available or tell the adult it is needed. If unsure, point to the job list, ask a short question, rephrase, offer a choice and model only the first needed action. Parallel recheck: a tray has a sheet and help card but no pencil.
Common errors

A finished tray alone does not show who prepared or checked it. Observe the actions. A missing item does not require pretending the job is done: reporting the need is responsible. Do not reward speed over safe work or call adult-completed actions independent.

Before and during the lesson

Prepare one light work tray per learner, plain sheets, suitable pencils and printed help cards. Keep supplies within easy reach. Set an accessible place for each finished tray and a separate adult model tray. Plan the real follow-on task: each learner uses a prepared tray to draw one simple shape or make a chosen mark; the help card is available to request support. Print the two Evidence Sheet and two Support Cards pages and a Vocabulary Mat.

Agree a small, safe class job with a clear finish point. Use light trays and ordinary checked stationery in an accessible work area. Adults manage any heavy item, high storage, spill or unsafe equipment. Do not use personal records or real names. A request for help is a responsible action, not failure. Respect a pause or adapted role; record what the learner did and what an adult completed. A group result does not prove that each learner completed the job.

Give each learner one tray and a clear reachable supply area. Observe collecting, placing, checking and reporting individually. Offer the prompt ladder and usual aid. Record the learner’s actions separately from adult completion. Allow a responsible report of an unfinished need; do not treat a polished tray as the only evidence.

The supplied job is resource preparation for an actual task within the lesson. If a different class job is used, staff record its exact brief, finish point, safety arrangements and observed learner actions. A role-card discussion alone does not establish responsibility for carrying out a job.
Evidence decisions
A dated observation of each learner preparing a work tray, checking it against the job card and reporting ready or a remaining need; actual actions, prompts, adult help and a next step are recorded.

Record observed with stated help, partial or not yet observed. Keep first work, exact prompts, adult actions and later responses separate. Unseen steps remain gaps. No total score or qualification result is inferred.
